patches.value: For the real mean-zero normalized 2*pi-periodic source equation U_t=U U_x+U_xxx, use the source twisted coefficients y_k(t)=exp(i*k^3*t) hat U(k,t), k!=0, with ||y||_(dot H^s)^2=sum_(k!=0)|k|^(2*s)|y_k|^2. for s>=0, finite T_s>0, initial dot H^s datum y0 and an upper bound B0 for its L2 norm, the source Galerkin flows have sup_[0,T_s] dot H^s norm bounded by a constant depending only on s,T_s,||y0||_(dot H^s),B0, uniformly in Galerkin dimension. For s>0 a subsequence converges to a distributional limiting solution with the same bound (the limiting statement uses strong L^p_t H^sigma convergence for 0<sigma<s and 1<p<infinity and weak-star L^infinity_t dot H^s convergence). The uniqueness and continuity claims for s>1/2 and for 0<s<=1/2 make this solution unique, C([0,T_s];dot H^s), L2 conserving and Lipschitz continuous in the initial dot H^s data. At s=0, for s=0 there is a unique C([0,T_s];dot H^0) solution obtained by smooth approximation and Lipschitz continuous in the initial data. For the two-flow estimate, for theta in (-1,0], if ||y0||_2+||z0||_2<=B, then their two source twisted flows satisfy sup_[0,T_s]||y-z||_(dot H^theta)<=C'(B,theta)*C_B(theta)^(T_s)*||y0-z0||_(dot H^theta). All these claims concern the source equation and its twist, not the target sign convention.

Let alpha_s in [0,1] and 0<=a_s<=b_s with b_s-a_s<=1. For three functions g_j in L^infinity([a_s,b_s];H^alpha_s) with partial_t g_j in L^infinity([a_s,b_s];H^(-23/14)), define Csrc(g1,g2,g3)=integral_(a_s)^(b_s) exp(t partial_x^3) Pnz{Pnz[(exp(-t partial_x^3)g1)(exp(-t partial_x^3)g2)]*(exp(-t partial_x^3)Dinv g3)}dt. With source unnormalized norms and ||g||_Xsrc=||g||_(L^infinity L2src)+||g'||_(L^infinity Hsrc^(-23/14)), the source gives ||Csrc||_(L2src)<=C*(b_s-a_s)*product_j||g_j||_Xsrc+C*||g_i||_(L^infinity Hsrc^(-23/14))*product_(j!=i)||g_j||_(L^infinity L2src) for each i=1,2,3. If the three inputs are time-independent then ||Csrc||_(L2src)<=C_alpha_s*(b_s-a_s)^alpha_s*product_j||g_j||_(Hsrc^alpha_s). Constants are independent of interval location and Fourier support.

Let 0<sigma_s<=1, tau_s>0, t_j=j*tau_s>=0 and t in [t_j,t_j+tau_s]. For time-independent mean-zero g1,g2 in Hsrc^sigma_s define Fsrc_j(t;g1,g2)=(1/2)integral_(t_j)^t exp(s partial_x^3)*partial_x[(exp(-s partial_x^3)g1)(exp(-s partial_x^3)g2)]ds. With beta0=2*sigma_s-3/2 for sigma_s<1/2, beta0=-1/2-epsilon for sigma_s=1/2 (any fixed sufficiently small epsilon>0), and beta0=sigma_s-1 for sigma_s>1/2, the source gives, for beta in [beta0,1+sigma_s], ||Fsrc_j(t;g1,g2)||_(Hsrc^beta)<=C*tau_s^((1+sigma_s-beta)/(1+sigma_s-beta0))*||g1||_(Hsrc^sigma_s)*||g2||_(Hsrc^sigma_s), with C depending only on exponents (and epsilon) and uniform in j,tau_s,t and support. Its endpoint formula is (1/6)[S_(-s) Pnz((S_s Dinv g1)(S_s Dinv g2))]_(s=t_j)^(s=t).

For sigma_s in [0,1], ||g*h||_(L2src)<=C_sigma_s ||g||_(Hsrc^sigma_s)||h||_(Hsrc^a(sigma_s)), where a(0)=1/2+epsilon, a(sigma_s)=1/2-sigma_s for 0<sigma_s<1/2, a(1/2)=epsilon, and a(sigma_s)=0 for 1/2<sigma_s<=1, with any fixed sufficiently small epsilon>0 at the indicated endpoints. The functions are arbitrary periodic functions in these two spaces; constants depend only on the chosen exponents.

For the source mean-zero smooth scheme, equivalently Psi after exp(-t partial_x^3)=S_t, and t_j=j*tau_s, write f=exp(t_j partial_x^3)u^j and Fsrc_j(t;f)=(1/2)integral_(t_j)^t Bop_s(f,f)ds, Asrc_j(f)=integral_(t_j)^(t_j+tau_s)Bop_s(f,Fsrc_j(s;f))ds. The source identities imply exactly exp((t_j+tau_s)partial_x^3)u^(j+1)=f+Fsrc_j(t_j+tau_s;f)+Asrc_j(f)-Rsrc_j(f,f,f). Here Rsrc_j has zero output at k=0 and, for k!=0, coefficient -tau_s/(18*i*k) sum_(a+b+c=k,a+b!=0) exp(-i*t_j*(k^3-a^3-b^3-c^3))*eta_(tau_s)(3*a*b*(a+b),3*k*c*(a+b))*hat f(a)*hat f(b)*hat f(c). This is the remainder in the source's trilinear definition, and is Remainder_(t_j,tau_s) under the displayed identifications. No convergence estimate is part of this identity.
